title: Molecular Dynamics Study on Wear Resistance of High Entropy Alloy Coatings Considering the Effect of Temperature

recollection.starting_material: guess: equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn high-entropy alloy coating
recollection.intervention: guess: molecular dynamics sliding wear simulations under a rigid diamond indenter at multiple temperatures (300 K, 600 K, 900 K)
recollection.structure: guess: nanocrystalline fcc solid-solution grains (~5 nm average size) in the coating
recollection.mechanism: guess: elevated temperature enhances atomic diffusion and dislocation activity, reducing local stress but increasing material removal under sliding
recollection.results: guess: coefficient of friction rises from ~0.20 at 300 K to ~0.35 at 900 K; wear volume increases by ~3× over the same range; estimated activation energy for dislocation motion ~1.0 eV

score.note: The recollection broadly identifies temperature-dependent MD wear/indentation simulations and several correct temperatures, but omits 1200 K and the loading protocol while adding an unsupported diamond indenter. The alloy composition and nanocrystalline structure are wrong. The proposed diffusion/dislocation mechanism does not match the reported dislocation-density reduction, lattice disorder, and stacking-fault transition. The friction, wear-volume, and activation-energy values are unsupported and omit the actual hardness and modulus results.
